US Stock Futures Fall as Iran Tensions, Higher Oil and AI Concerns Weigh: Dow Jones, S&P, Nasdaq, Wall Street

Large US flag on New York Stock Exchange ©bones64

US stock futures moved lower on Monday as investors assessed developments in the conflict involving Iran, higher oil prices and OpenAI's decision to pause training of its latest artificial intelligence models.

At 03:50 ET, S&P 500 futures were down 0.42% at 7,710.7 points, while Nasdaq 100 futures declined 1% to 30,595 points. Dow Jones futures were down 0.4%. The broader decline in US futures and the near-1% fall in Nasdaq futures were also reported during Asian trading.

The moves followed US President Donald Trump's rejection of an Iranian proposal concerning the Strait of Hormuz and an end to the fighting, while technology sentiment was affected by developments surrounding OpenAI's advanced models.

Iran Maintains Conditions for Reopening Strait of Hormuz

Iran said diplomacy remained the only way to resolve its conflict with the United States and Israel after Trump rejected Tehran's proposal concerning the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to hostilities.

Iran presented its proposal during the United Nations General Assembly in New York. Trump rejected the proposal and said Iran was seeking an agreement because of its position in the conflict.

Trump said Iran wanted an agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz immediately because it was "losing so badly."

Iran subsequently maintained its conditions for reopening the waterway, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying that any move to reopen the strait remained conditional on those requirements being met.

Trump has nevertheless indicated that he expects further talks with Iran during the week.

Oil Prices Rise as Hormuz Uncertainty Continues

Oil prices moved higher as uncertainty continued over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude futures rose 1.1% to $105.48 a barrel, while WTI crude futures gained 0.8% to $93.12.

The Strait of Hormuz is an important route for global energy shipments, making the timing and extent of any reopening a focus for commodity and financial markets.

A prolonged period of higher crude prices could contribute to higher fuel and transportation costs, although the eventual impact on inflation and monetary policy would depend on the duration and scale of the increase and other economic conditions.

OpenAI Pauses Training of Latest AI Models

Technology stocks were also in focus after OpenAI paused training of its latest artificial intelligence models while reviewing safeguards following incidents involving AI agents interacting with US government websites in unexpected ways.

The company said the agents had carried out actions beyond their assigned tasks while gathering and distributing publicly available information. Officials said there was no evidence that non-public information had been accessed in the incidents described.

AI Skeptics Surrender Again as Traders Eye Path Forward for Tech
Bloomberg · Bloomberg
Jessica Menton
Wed, September 23, 2026 at 6:27 AM MDT 4 min read
^NDX

(Bloomberg) -- The road to the Nasdaq 100 Index's first record since June was anything but straightforward. Now the equity bulls that helped drive the move are looking for evidence that momentum won't peter out.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Nvidia's Stock Is Flashing a Warning Sign as Valuation Drops

Apple Developing New Fitness Tracker Aimed at Rivaling Whoop

Trump Hails Iran Talks Even as Tehran Sets 'Firm Positions'

Dangote Hires Engineers India for $16 Billion Kenya Refinery

Meta's Muse Drags Down Stocks That Depend on 'Consumer Inertia'

They've added $22 billion into technology-focused US exchange-traded funds this quarter, compared with $4.6 billion into the rest of the market, data compiled by Bloomberg Intelligence show. And more recently, hedge funds boosted their net-long Nasdaq 100 futures positions to the highest level since December, according to the latest data from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

While the advance in the tech-heavy gauge has been stellar and earnings robust, uncertainty around tensions in the Middle East, persistent inflation and the Federal Reserve's efforts to tame it still linger. And with so much riding on the AI trade, the setup suggests little room for error.

"Investors still feel optimistic about AI given that corporate earnings are really strong," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management in St. Louis, whose firm is overweight cyber security, software and chip stocks and underweight sectors including consumer staples and real estate. "But we need to continue to see upward earnings estimate revisions for the biggest tech companies for the rally to continue."

The Nasdaq 100 gained 0.8% on Tuesday, closing at a record high and reversing a brutal stretch earlier this year that pushed the gauge down more than 10% from its peak. The S&P 500 Index closed little changed on and is within 0.5% from reclaiming its record in August.

And Wall Street is positioning for the rally to continue. US stocks saw the largest net buying in five weeks last week, with software firms leading the charge, according to Goldman Sachs Prime Services. US equity funds attracted nearly $64 billion in weekly flows through Sept. 16, the most in three months, according to Bank of America strategists citing EPFR Global data. Cash, meanwhile, had the largest outflow in nine weeks.

"The AI rally still has more room to run and we don't see investors pulling back on risk anytime soon," Athanasios Psarofagis, an ETF analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, said by phone. "The flows into tech stocks isn't anywhere near extreme yet to be a contrarian indicator to dump those stocks. It's very hard to derail this momentum. The show goes on."

(Bloomberg) -- A relentless tech-stock rally pushed the Nasdaq 100 Index toward its first record since June on Tuesday, extending gains fueled by bets on artificial intelligence tools from the likes of Meta Platforms Inc.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Paramount to Settle Lawsuits, Paving Way for Warner Bros.

Nvidia's Stock Is Flashing a Warning Sign as Valuation Falls

Qatar Energy Chief Says Bessent 'Wrong' About Hormuz Future

Stocks Jump on AI Optimism as AMD Tops $1 Trillion: Markets Wrap

AI Risk Is Everywhere and It's Making Billion Dollar Funds Nervous

The tech-heavy gauge advanced as much as 0.7% to 30,699, a level that exceededd its record close in June, before paring the gains. Shopify Inc. was the top-performing stock in the Nasdaq 100, climbing 7.0% after inking a partnership with Meta for its Muse AI product.

Trades rushed back into technology and growth stocks seen as the biggest beneficiaries from AI amid renewed hopes for diplomatic efforts to revive energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz. The S&P 500 Index traded little changed and is hovering 0.5% away from its record in August, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.4%.

"What a rally," said Brad Conger, chief investment officer at Hirtle & Co. "For the past month or so I've felt like the market was incredibly strong even though it wasn't moving anywhere because it was coping with oil going up."

In the current market, investors are "more than willing to chase rallies when they occur," said Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers LLC. He added that investors have been unwilling to jump out of the tech sector. "During the modest selling occurred last week, it felt as though investors were only willing to lighten up, not truly liquidate their positions or take risk out of their portfolios."

Strategists see more bullishness in the AI trade even as a rally in chipmakers in Europe and Asia stalled overnight. Separately, Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. unveiled what it called China's most powerful AI chip, potentially enhancing competition with the US sector.

"The strong reception for Muse reignited enthusiasm across the AI hardware ecosystem," said Christopher Murphy, co-head of derivatives strategy at Susquehanna. He added that options flows signal "upside chasing" in the tech trade.

Energy stocks were broadly down as oil continued to slide after overnight headlines in Japan revealed that Iranian officials had proposed re-opening the Strait of Hormuz in seven days. Saudi Arabia also expects to resume operations on its 7-million-barrels-a-day East-West pipeline this week.
